The '''Lithuanian Mathematical Society''' or '''LMS''' (Lithuanian: {{lang|lt|Lietuvos matematikų draugija}}, LMD) is a [[mathematical society]] founded in 1962.
The LMS is based in [[Vilnius]],{{r|kontaktai}} and is a founding member of the [[European Mathematical Society]].{{r|ems|ems2020}} It is a full member of the [[International Mathematical Union]].{{r|imu}}

==History==
Lithuania was a part of the [[Russian Empire]] from 1795 to 1914.
The [[Lithuanian press ban]], in force from 1865 to 1904, forbade the publication of material using the [[Latin alphabet]] in the Russian Empire, which made it harder to publish in [[Lithuanian language|Lithuanian]].{{r|britannica}}
Shortly after the ban was lifted, the Lithuanian Learned Society was founded in 1907, which counted some mathematicians as members.{{r|ems2020}}
From 1918 to 1940 Lithuania was an independent state, though [[Vilnius]] was occupied by Poland, and in this period the Lithuanian Society of Teachers of Mathematics and Physics was active in improving mathematics education.{{r|Kubilius|ems2020}}

In 1940 Lithuania was occupied by the [[Soviet Union]], and in 1941 it was invaded by the Nazis as part of [[Operation Barbarossa]].{{r|ems2020}}
Many teachers and professors fled Lithuania;{{r|ems2020}} after the [[Second World War]] the country became the [[Lithuanian Soviet Socialist Republic]], and remained a part of the Soviet Union until 1990.

The most significant Lithuanian mathematician of the Soviet period was [[Jonas Kubilius]].
Kubilius was born close to [[Eržvilkas]], studied mathematics at [[Vilnius University]] from 1939 to 1946, and obtained his PhD from [[Leningrad University]] in 1951.{{r|Kubilius}}
Kubilius returned to Lithuania in 1951 and began working at the [[Lithuanian Academy of Sciences]].{{r|ems2020}}
He played a role in the formation of the Institute of Physics and Mathematics in 1956, and became an assistant director, leading the Division of Mathematics.{{r|Kubilius}}

In 1958 Kubilius became rector of Vilnius University,{{r|ems2020}} replacing [[Juozas Bulavas]] who had been removed for trying to reduce Soviet influence on the university.{{r|Kubilius}}
The same year, the Institute of Physics and Mathematics held its first annual mathematics conference, where the idea of a national mathematical society was raised, and a working group was appointed to write its statutes.{{r|ems2020}}
Kubilius' international reputation as a mathematician was growing, and the Soviets allowed the creation of the society.{{r|ems2020}}
The Lithuanian Mathematical Society registered its statutes on 3 February 1962 under the patronage of the Lithuanian Academy of Sciences; it did not become fully independent until 2014.{{r|ems2020}}
Kubilius served as the president of the society from its founding until his death in 2011.{{r|ems2020}}

==Publications==
The LMS was involved in the founding of the ''{{ill|Lithuanian Mathematical Journal|nl}}'' in 1961, which since 2008 has been published by [[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]].{{r|ems2020|journal}}
Together with [[Vilnius University]], the LMS publishes ''{{ill|Lietuvos matematikos rinkinys|lt}}'', a journal of research mathematics in both Lithuanian and English.{{r|rinkinys}}
From 1996 to 2003 the LMS published the journal ''α+ω'', which billed itself as "a magazine for teachers, pupils, students and teachers of mathematics and computer science, for anyone interested in the problems, history and development of mathematics."{{r|alpha}}

==Prizes==
The Lithuanian Mathematical Society biennially awards its Young Mathematicians Prize (Lithuanian: {{lang|lt|jaunųjų matematikų premija}}) to a Lithuanian mathematician under the age of 40.{{r|young-prize}}
Past winners are:
*2016 {{ndash}} Vytautas Paškūnas{{r|young-prize-2016}}
*2018 {{ndash}} Kęstutis Česnavičius{{r|young-prize-2018}}
*2020 {{ndash}} Paulius Drungilas{{r|young-prize-2020}}
*2022 {{ndash}} Vidas Regelskis{{r|young-prize-all}}
*2024 – Matas Šileikis{{r|young-prize-all}}

The Zigmas Žemaitis Medal of the LMS is awarded for contributions to science and education in Lithuania; it is named for Lithuanian mathematician {{ill|Zigmas Žemaitis|lt}}.{{r|ems2020|zigmas-medal}}

==Presidents==
The past presidents of the Lithuanian Mathematical Society are:{{r|ems2020}}
*[[Jonas Kubilius]] (1962–2011)
*{{ill|Eugenijus Manstavičius|lt}} (2011–2014)
*{{ill|Remigijus Leipus|lt}} (2014–2021)
*Artūras Štikonas (2021–present){{r|home}}
